note: Part B (drawing) is not transcribed: no model answer exists.

questions.text: A pyramid with a base side 6 cm and height 7 cm is merged with a cube of length 5 cm such that the centroid of the cube matches with the centre of the base of the pyramid. The base of the pyramid is parallel to the base of the cube and the edges of the base of the pyramid are parallel to the sides of the cube. Count the number surfaces in the resulting solid.
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: The cube's centre is at the centre of the pyramid's base, so the 6 cm base sits at the cube's mid-height and sticks out 0.5 cm beyond each 5 cm side. The pyramid's slant faces pass back inside the cube at a height of \(7/6\) cm above the base and come out through the top face at 2.5 cm. Surfaces: cube bottom 1, cube top (with a square hole) 1, each of the 4 cube sides is cut into a lower and an upper part, so 8, the underside ring of the pyramid base 1, 4 slanting strips just above that ring, and 4 triangles of the pyramid tip above the cube. Total \(1+1+8+1+4+4=19\).

questions.text: How many different types of symbols appear in the figure given below?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: List each distinct symbol once while scanning row by row: dotted circle, solid circle, ring, triangle, filled square, hollow square frame, square with a filled inner square, triple concentric squares, filled diamond, diamond with a dot, double hollow diamond, pentagon, hexagon, octagon, plus sign, X, thick six-arm asterisk, thick five-arm asterisk, thin eight-arm asterisk, thin three-arm star, four-point star, concave four-point star, five-point star, six-point star, eight-point star and many-pointed starburst. That makes 26 types.

questions.text: The numbers in the hexagon groups are arranged in a particular order. Find the number which would replace the question mark.
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: Read each row of a group as a four-digit number. In every group, row 2 minus row 1 equals row 3 minus row 4: 8659 - 6849 = 1810 = 4675 - 2865; 9299 - 5777 = 3522 = 5658 - 2136; 4595 - 4271 = 324 = 6005 - 5681. In the last group 4492 - 3284 = 1208, so row 3 must be 6844 + 1208 = 8052, and the missing digit is 8.

questions.text: What is the maximum number of equilateral triangles of side 3 cm that can be fitted in a large equilateral triangle with length 11.2 cm?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Area alone gives an upper bound: the large triangle has (11.2 / 3)^2, about 13.9 times the area of a small one, so at most 13 fit. The real number is lower because whole triangles of side 3 must fit inside the edges. Rows of upright and inverted triangles fill a side of 9 cm, and the leftover strip along the edges takes a few more when the triangles are placed carefully. IIT Bombay's final key gives 11.

questions.text: The figure given below is to be cloned twice. The first clone on the right is to be reflected across the OP axis. The second clone on the left is to be reflected across the MN axis. The resultant figure is then to be cloned and reflected across the QR axis. Count the number of triangles in the final figure.
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: The figure is symmetric, so the two clones are copies placed side by side to the left and right, and the whole row is then mirrored below QR. One copy has 6 triangles: the big upper triangle, the big lower triangle and the 4 small ones inside it. Each joint between two copies adds one upside-down small triangle (2 per row), so each row of three copies has 20. Slanted lines of the top row continue straight into the mirrored row through QR, which creates 10 more triangles that cross QR. Total \(20 + 20 + 10 = 50\).

questions.text:
A company account book reveals the following figures:

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Sales | 2,35,126 |
| Gross Profit | 68,799 |
| Administrative Expenses | 2,456 |
| Selling Expenses | 4,789 |

Calculate the Operating Profit Ratio of the company.
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: Operating profit is gross profit less the operating expenses: 68,799 - 2,456 - 4,789 = 61,554. The operating profit ratio is operating profit divided by sales: 61,554 / 2,35,126 = 0.2618, that is about 26.18%.
questions.defect: IIT Bombay's final key accepts the ratio written either as a fraction (0.26 to 0.27) or as a percentage (26 to 27). The answer stored here is the fraction.

questions.text: How many different ways are there to get from Tile A to Tile I without visiting a tile more than once, if only horizontal and vertical movements are allowed?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Count routes from A (bottom-left) to I (top-right) that never revisit a tile. By symmetry, count the routes that start A to B and double. From B: B-C-F-I, B-C-F-E-H-I, B-C-F-E-D-G-H-I, B-E-F-I, B-E-H-I, B-E-D-G-H-I gives 6. So the total is \(2 \times 6 = 12\).

questions.text: There are some men and some women in a group. Each person shakes hands with exactly one other person in the entire group. After this round of handshakes, eight men and four women find that they shook hands with someone of the same sex. The total number of handshakes exchanged in the entire group is 87. At most how many women can there possibly be in this group?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: Everyone shakes exactly one hand, so 87 handshakes means 87 pairs and 174 people. Eight men with men make 4 man-man pairs and four women with women make 2 woman-woman pairs. The remaining \(87 - 4 - 2 = 81\) pairs are man-woman. Women \(= 4 + 81 = 85\).

questions.text: It is 12 o’clock, and the hour and minute hands are aligned exactly one over the other. Both hands move continuously. After how many minutes will they meet again?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: The minute hand gains \(6 - 0.5 = 5.5\) degrees a minute on the hour hand. To meet again it must gain 360 degrees, which takes \(360 / 5.5 = 720/11\) minutes, about 65.45 minutes.

questions.text: At most how many spheres of the same size can be placed around a same size sphere at the centre so that they all simultaneously touch the sphere at the centre?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: This is the kissing number in three dimensions: at most 12 equal spheres can touch a central sphere of the same size at once, as in a close-packed stack of oranges.

questions.text: A water tank of dimensions 20 cm x 5 cm x 10 cm has 307 cc water in it. A few bricks, each of dimensions 5 cm x 2 cm x 1 cm are fully submerged in the tank. Each brick absorbs 30% of its own volume of water. Just enough bricks are put in, such that the water level rises to completely fill the tank. How many bricks were put in the tank?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: Tank volume = \(20 \times 5 \times 10 = 1000\) cc. Each brick takes 10 cc of space but soaks up 3 cc of the water, so each brick raises the filled volume by \(10 - 3 = 7\) cc. We need \(1000 - 307 = 693\) cc more, so \(693 / 7 = 99\) bricks.

questions.text: Count the total number of black diamonds in the given pattern.
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Count every black diamond in the pattern, including the ones lying on their side between the upright ones, and do not count the half-diamonds cut off at the edges. The 8 upright black diamonds and the 4 lying on their side make 12.

questions.text: How many pages of size 21 cm x 25 cm can be made from a roll of 48 m x 1.2 m paper? Assume the pages are perfectly cut edge to edge.
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: The roll is 4800 cm by 120 cm. Split the 120 cm width into three 25 cm strips and two 21 cm strips (\(75 + 42 = 117\) cm). A 25 cm strip holds pages with their 21 cm side along the roll: 228 pages (\(228 \times 21 = 4788\)). A 21 cm strip holds pages with their 25 cm side along the roll: \(4800/25 = 192\). Total \(3 \times 228 + 2 \times 192 = 1068\), better than all pages one way (960).

questions.text: How many tree trunks are there in the given figure?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Count each trunk where it meets the ground, working from one side of the picture to the other, and count a trunk once even where branches or other trunks cross in front of it. IIT Bombay's final key accepts 21 or 22.

questions.text: Shown below is a quadrant of a disc with cut-outs. Find the total number of cut-outs in the complete disc.
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Each quadrant has 6 cut-outs fully inside it: 2 squares, 2 small circles, the half-disc cut by the diagonal and the quarter-ring cut near the corner, giving \(4 \times 6 = 24\). The half-circles and the triangular notches on the straight edges join the matching halves of the next quadrant, giving 4 circles and 4 diamonds. The small square notch at the centre joins up into 1 central square. Total \(24 + 4 + 4 + 1 = 33\).

questions.text: Count the number of people in this picture who are wearing spectacles.
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Go through the crowd row by row and tick off each person whose spectacles sit on their eyes, including sunglasses; check small faces at the back carefully. IIT Bombay's final key gives 26.

questions.text: You have been given a calculator that looks as in the image below. Given that you are allowed a total of only 6 key entries of which you MUST use at least one key entry for an operator and another key entry for the ‘equals to’ symbol, what is the largest number you can calculate?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: Four of the six key presses are left for numbers after one operator and one equals. The 00 key gives two digits in one press, so 9 then 00 makes 900 with two presses. \(900 \times 900 =\) uses exactly six presses and gives 810000; other splits such as \(9900 \times 9\) (89100) or \(99 \times 99\) (9801) are smaller.

questions.text: Count the number of fonts used in the given set of words.
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Group the words by the shapes of their letters, not by size or weight: compare serifs, the contrast between thick and thin strokes, the ends of strokes and letters such as a, g and e. A word in the same design at a different size or weight belongs to the same font. IIT Bombay's final key gives 10 fonts.

questions.text: There are a host of HTTP codes which communicate different server messages: 404 for “not found”, 403 for “forbidden” and so on. Recently there has been a proposal to assign a code for “censored/censorship” in honour of the author Ray Bradbury. What is the proposed code?
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: HTTP 451 ('Unavailable For Legal Reasons') was proposed for content blocked for legal reasons or censorship. The number refers to Ray Bradbury's novel Fahrenheit 451, about a society that burns books.

questions.text: Two friends, one on a bike and the other in a car, arrive together at a parking lot. The chance that the one in the car will find a parking space is 0.1, and the one on the bike not finding a parking space is 0.1. What is the probability that only one of them finds a parking space?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: The car finds a space with probability 0.1; the bike fails with probability 0.1, so it finds one with probability 0.9. Only one finds a space: car yes and bike no gives \(0.1 \times 0.1 = 0.01\); car no and bike yes gives \(0.9 \times 0.9 = 0.81\). Total 0.82.

questions.text: Select all statements about the Silk Route that are TRUE:

options.label: A
options.text: The Silk Route derives its name from the lucrative trade in Indian silks carried out along its length, beginning from the 3rd century BCE.

options.label: B
options.text: Some scholars prefer the term “Silk Routes” because the road included an extensive network of routes, even though few were more than rough caravan tracks.

options.label: C
options.text: Soon after the Roman conquest of Egypt in 30 BCE, communications and trade between China, Southeast Asia, India, the Middle East, Africa and Europe blossomed on an unprecedented scale because of the Silk Route.

options.label: D
options.text: The Buddhist movement was perhaps the first large-scale missionary movement in the history of world religions, and its transmission to the Mediterranean began via the Silk Route in the 1st century CE.

questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: B is true: the 'road' was really a network of routes, many of them rough caravan tracks. C is true: after Rome took Egypt in 30 BCE, trade linking China, India, the Middle East, Africa and Europe grew on a new scale. A is false: the name comes from Chinese silk, and the term was coined only in the 19th century. D is false: Buddhism spread along the route mainly eastwards into China from about the 1st century CE, not to the Mediterranean.

questions.text:
There are no precise rules about punctuation (Fowler lays out some general advice (as best he can under the complex circumstances of English prose (he points out, for example, that we possess only four stops (the comma, the semicolon, the colon and the period (the question mark and exclamation point are not, strictly speaking, stops; they are indicators of tone (oddly enough, the Greeks employed the semicolon for their question mark (it produces a strange sensation to read a Greek sentence which is a straightforward question: Why weepest thou; (instead of Why weepest thou? (and, of course, there are parentheses (which are surely a kind of punctuation making this whole matter much more complicated by having to count up the left- handed parentheses in order to be sure of closing with the right number (but if the parentheses were left out, with nothing to work with but the stops, we would have considerably more flexibility in the deploying of layers of meaning than if we tried to separate all the clauses by physical barriers (and in the latter case, while we might have more precision and exactitude for our meaning, we would lose the essential flavour of language, which is its wonderful ambiguity.

Which of the following statements is/are true of the paragraph above?

options.label: A
options.text: The thesis statement of the above paragraph is that there are no precise rules about punctuation.

options.label: B
options.text: The author asserts that the Greeks were confused about their punctuation; they used semicolons in place of question marks.

options.label: C
options.text: The recursive nesting of subordinate clauses within parentheses in the above paragraph simplifies sentence structure and clarifies writing.

options.label: D
options.text: The author argues that parentheses may offer the possibility of greater rigor and accuracy for our meaning, but they do so at the cost of a critical quality of language, which is its wonderful ambiguity.

questions.subject: Language
questions.solution: A is true: the opening claim that there are no precise rules about punctuation is the point the playful paragraph then demonstrates. D is true: the last clause says separating clauses by physical barriers gives precision and exactitude but loses the wonderful ambiguity of language. B is false: the Greeks' semicolon is mentioned as an oddity, not as confusion. C is false: the nesting makes the sentence more complicated, which is the joke.

questions.text:
It is now theoretically possible to recreate an identical creature from any animal or plant, from the DNA contained in the nucleus of any somatic cell. A single plant root-tip cell can be teased and seduced into conceiving a perfect copy of the whole plant; a frog’s intestinal epithelial cell possesses the complete instructions needed for a new, same frog. If the technology were further advanced, you could do this with a human being, and there are now startled predictions all over the place that this will in fact be done, someday, in order to provide a version of immortality for carefully selected, especially valuable people.

The cloning of humans is on most of the lists of things to worry about from Science, along with behavior control, genetic engineering, transplanted heads, computer poetry, and the unrestrained growth of plastic flowers.

…

The public questions are obvious. Who is to be selected, and on what qualifications? How to handle the risks of misused technology, such as self-determined cloning by the rich and powerful but socially objectionable, or the cloning by governments of dumb, docile masses for the world’s work? What will be the effect on all the uncloned rest of us of human sameness? After all, we’ve accustomed ourselves through hundreds of millennia to the continual exhilaration of uniqueness; each of us is totally different, in a fundamental sense, from all the other [seven] billion. Selfness is an essential fact of life. The thought of human nonselfness, precise sameness, is terrifying, when you think about it.

Which of the following statements is/are true of the paragraph above?

options.label: A
options.text: The arc of this passage moves from the biological to the social and the metaphysical—connecting the concerns of cloning with issues of identity and self-hood.

options.label: B
options.text: The author takes the view that cloning broadens the understanding of humanness by making room for evolving modifications in human beings and societies.

options.label: C
options.text: The author believes that if they are not socially objectionable, the self-determined cloning by the rich and powerful would not be a misuse of technology.

options.label: D
options.text: Were cloning permitted, the author is tormented by the prospect of the loss of selfness or uniqueness which, according to him, is at the very core of our sense of self.

questions.subject: Language
questions.solution: A is true: the passage starts with cells and DNA, moves to public questions about who is cloned and how, and ends on selfness and identity. D is true: the author calls the thought of human sameness terrifying because uniqueness is an essential fact of life. B is false: the author worries about cloning rather than praising it. C is false: cloning by the rich and powerful is listed as a risk of misuse, not excused.

questions.text:
In a wildlife rescue and rehabilitation centre in the Northeast of India, there are six orphaned creatures—ages 1.5 months to 6 months—who are currently receiving care, and await release into the wild in due course. They are an elephant, a rhinoceros, a wild buffalo, a clouded leopard, a swamp deer, and a hog badger. They were found in four different kinds of perilous situations, including a flooded ditch, attacks by poachers that killed the mother, a river in spate, and dangerous proximity to human habitat. After a few weeks in the rescue centre, each creature demonstrated one characteristic trait that stood out above all others: one was mischievous, another aggressive, a third shy, the fourth retiring, one fretful and the last one frisky.

Three creatures were actively injured.
The wild buffalo, who was found in a flooded ditch, is aggressive.
The creatures found in the river in spate are the mischievous and the fretful ones.
One of the two found in the flooded ditch is actively injured, while two of the uninjured, but severely stressed were found in the river in spate and as a victim of attack by poachers, respectively.
The shy creature was rescued from close to human habitat.
The swamp deer is fretful, and is actively injured.
The rhinoceres was found in a flooded ditch, and the clouded leopard was a victim of attack by poachers.
The elephant is mischievous and severely stressed.

Which of the following assertions is/are true?

options.label: A
options.text: If the creature who has a retiring temperament is uninjured, then the frisky creature is a clouded leopard.

options.label: B
options.text: The hog badger is shy, and was found close to human habitat.

options.label: C
options.text: If the creature who is aggressive by temperament is actively injured, then so is the one who is, by nature, retiring.

questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: The buffalo and rhinoceros are the two in the ditch; the elephant (mischievous) and swamp deer (fretful) are in the river; the leopard is the poachers' victim, so the hog badger must be the shy one from near human habitat. The elephant and the leopard are uninjured, and so is one of the two ditch animals, so the injured three are the deer, the hog badger and the other ditch animal. The rhinoceros and leopard are retiring and frisky in some order. So B and D are true. A fails because the retiring one could be the leopard (always uninjured) with the rhinoceros frisky; C fails because if the buffalo is injured, the rhinoceros and the leopard are both uninjured.

questions.text:
From the options at bottom, select the Indian author/s writing in English whose works are represented below:

i. Circle of Reason
ii. Shadow Lines
iii. Prison and Chocolate Cake
iv. Nectar in a Sieve
v. Roots and Shadows
vi. That long silence
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: The Circle of Reason and The Shadow Lines are by Amitav Ghosh. Prison and Chocolate Cake is Nayantara Sahgal's memoir. Roots and Shadows and That Long Silence are by Shashi Deshpande. Nectar in a Sieve is by Kamala Markandaya, who is not an option, and Namita Gokhale wrote none of these.

questions.text: A recent survey among concertgoers found that smaller, older halls sound better for symphony orchestras, as compared to bigger, modern ones. What is/are the reason(s) for this?

options.label: A
options.text: Smaller halls are better able to reflect bass notes from the side walls and the ceiling, which is an important factor in the quality of symphony sound.

options.label: B
options.text: Old halls are a part of history and heritage, so people think they sound better.

options.label: C
options.text: Old concert halls with good acoustics tend to get maintained and preserved, while ones with suboptimal acoustics get renovated or replaced.

options.label: D
options.text: The atmosphere is more intimate in an older concert hall—visually as well as acoustically—because the concertgoer is relatively close to the musicians.

questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: All four are reasons. A: in a smaller hall the side walls and ceiling are close, so bass notes reflect back to the listener and the sound feels full. B: people value old halls as heritage, and that colours how they judge the sound. C: old halls that sounded poor were rebuilt or demolished, so the old halls still standing are mostly the good ones. D: an older, smaller hall puts the listener close to the orchestra, which makes the experience more intimate.

questions.text: Identify which of the options given below can be folded to make the 3D object shown in the box.
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Count the unit squares on the surface of the solid, then check each net for the same number of squares and fold it in your mind square by square, making sure no two squares land on the same face. IIT Bombay's final key gives C.
questions.defect: As drawn, the solid is made of 6 cubes, so its surface has 26 unit squares, but each of the four nets has 25 squares, so none folds into it exactly. IIT Bombay's final key gives C, but the solid it intends cannot be settled from the printed figure.

questions.text: Which of the figures given below is/are simple rotations of the figure above.
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: The figure is a hexagon made of 24 small triangles, each holding an arrowhead. Turn each option back by its angle so that its edges line up with the original, then compare the arrowheads triangle by triangle. In A, B and D every one of the 24 arrowheads lands in the same triangle pointing the same way, so they are pure rotations. In C one arrowhead (in the upper half, next to the middle line) points a different way after turning, so C is not a rotation of the figure.

questions.text:
All doctors have to have a good understanding of the human body. Vijay has a good understanding of the human body. So he must be a cardiologist.

Which of the following options exhibit the exact same fallacy as the statement above.

options.label: A
options.text: All dentists have to have a good understanding of human teeth. Santosh really has a good understanding of human teeth. So he must be a medical practitioner.

options.label: B
options.text: All canines hunt in packs. Devil always hunts with his pack. So he must be a wolf.

options.label: C
options.text: All good artists have a good sense of colour. Sunita has an excellent sense of colour. So Sunita must be a painter.

options.label: D
options.text: All lecturers have to talk a lot. Vineet can talk for hours together. So he must be a teacher.

questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: The statement makes two leaps: from a trait shared by a group (doctors) it concludes that Vijay belongs to the group, and then narrows to one particular kind of member (a cardiologist is one kind of doctor). B does exactly this: from a trait of canines it concludes Devil is a wolf, one kind of canine. C does the same: from a trait of good artists it concludes Sunita is a painter, one kind of artist. A and D instead conclude a wider category (a dentist is already a medical practitioner, a lecturer is already a teacher), so their reasoning is not the same.

questions.text: Select the artwork(s) which is/are attributed to Leonardo Da Vinci:
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: A is the Virgin of the Rocks and C is the Mona Lisa, both painted by Leonardo da Vinci. B is the Madonna del Granduca by Raphael. D is a red chalk study of a male back and arm by Michelangelo, made for the Libyan Sibyl on the Sistine Chapel ceiling.

questions.text: Which of the following is a/are river(s):
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: The Alaknanda is a headstream of the Ganga in Uttarakhand, the Parvati flows through the Parvati valley in Himachal Pradesh (another Parvati flows in Madhya Pradesh) and the Vaigai flows past Madurai in Tamil Nadu. Baralacha La is a high mountain pass on the Manali to Leh road, not a river: 'La' means pass.

questions.text: A square is cut into 7 pieces, as shown on the extreme left of the image. Identify which of the options can be made using all 7 pieces.
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: The square is a tangram: two large triangles, one medium triangle, two small triangles, a square and a parallelogram, and each silhouette must use exactly these seven. A uses a square and two small triangles for the head and another small triangle for the tail, which needs three small triangles, so it is impossible. In D the head (square and two small triangles), body (two large triangles) and tail (parallelogram) leave the medium triangle out. B splits into two large triangles, the medium triangle, the parallelogram and a small triangle in the body, with the square as head and a small triangle as ear. C splits into two large triangles, the medium triangle and both small triangles, with the square as head and the parallelogram as ear.

questions.text: Identify which of the options given below can be folded to make the 3D object in the picture shown on the left.
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: A net of this object needs the two side profiles (mirror images of each other) joined by strips that wrap round the profile: the back, the faces of the slot, the steps and slopes and the curved front. Fold each option in your mind and check that every strip is as long as the edge of the profile it covers and that the slot's faces land inside the slot. A and D fold into the object; B and C put a face on the wrong side.

questions.text: Shown in the image are schematic diagrams of folding chair structures. If the black dots indicate a hinged joint, identify the structure(s) that will work as a folding chair.
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: A folding chair must hold its shape when someone sits on it and still fold flat when it is put away. Check each structure: a frame that is a rigid triangle cannot fold at all, and a frame with a loop of four or more bars needs something to lock it open, or it collapses under load. IIT Bombay's final key gives D as the only structure that does both.

questions.text: Shown below is a tyre tread mark. Choose the correct cross-section(s) that correspond(s) to the same tread mark. All cross sections are perpendicular to the tyre.
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: A cross-section perpendicular to the tyre is a slice straight across the band of the tread, and the grooves show as notches in it. Slide the slice along the tread mark and note the pattern of gaps at each position: one position gives the notches of A, another those of C and another those of D. B's notches do not occur anywhere along the mark.

questions.text:
Shown below are three thematic population age-sex pyramids of three countries. The horizontal axis represents population in millions and the vertical axis represents age cohorts for both male and female population.

Which of the following statements is/are correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Figure 2 depicts a low population growth, whereas it is high in figure 3.

options.label: B
options.text: Figure 1 and figure 2 are from developed nations.

questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: Figure 3 is a wide-based triangle: many births, and numbers fall steadily with age, which means high growth and low life expectancy (A and D). Figure 2 has nearly equal bars from bottom to top, a stationary population with low growth, typical of a developed nation. Figure 1 has a narrow base and a bulge in the middle and older ages, so fewer children are being born and the population is ageing, also a developed-nation pattern (B and C).

questions.text: Figure 1 shows a specific pattern. From the options below, select the pattern that best matches the one in Figure 1.
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: Figure 1 lists A A B C E H M. As positions in the alphabet these are 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, the Fibonacci series, where each term is the sum of the two before it. Option C nests shapes with 1 and 1 (two dots), 2 (a half circle, two sides), 3 (triangle), 5 (pentagon), 8 (octagon) and 13 (outer polygon) sides, the same series. The circles in B come in sizes 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, and the grid in A and the bars in D do not follow the series.

questions.text: Figure 1 below depicts the locations of 50 families. They are affiliated with red and blue parties as shown. Five wards are to be drawn such that they are continuous and have equal number of families. The party that wins three or more of the five wards wins the election. Select the option(s) such that the blue party wins.
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: The grid is 5 columns by 10 rows: 20 blue families in the two left columns and 30 red. Each ward must hold 10 families. In A the wards hold 12, 8, 10, 12 and 8 families and in C 10, 10, 9, 11 and 10, so they are not equal. B's five shapes cannot be fitted together into the 5 by 10 grid. D's shapes fit the grid, and three of its wards each take 6 blue and 4 red families, so blue wins three wards.

questions.text: Given below is a structure made of coloured straws. Which of the views shown in the options belong(s) to the object in the box?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: The structure has eight straws from the apex to the points of a base made of two overlapping squares. Going round the apex, the straw colours are green, blue, red, blue, yellow, red, yellow, red. A is the view from the top: this order appears clockwise and the base edges match. C is the view from below (its base straws lie in front of the apex straws), so the same order appears reversed, which is correct, and its base edges match too. B is a side view whose straws and base edges also match. D has two green apex straws and only one yellow, but the object has one green and two yellow, so D is not a view of it.

questions.text: Holes have been drilled through a cube of size 10 x 10 x 10 units, as shown in the figure below. The number near each hole indicates its depth in units. All holes, except A, B, C, D and P, have been sealed on the surface after drilling. If water is poured through hole P, from which of the holes A, B, C, D will it find its way out?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Place each hole on the 10 by 10 grid and extend it by its depth. P goes 7 units down from the top. Holes A and B run 7 and 6 units into the cube at P's lower levels, on either side of P's shaft and past it, so water from P passes into them and out. The 2 by 2 hole of depth 8 on the right face runs into P's shaft; the large hole of depth 8 on the top sits against it and reaches down onto the tunnel of D (depth 6), so water also leaves at D. C's tunnel meets only the sealed hole of depth 3, which joins nothing else, so no water comes out of C.

questions.text: Choose the option that comes next in the pattern sequence given below.
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Each figure has an outer ring of 12 symbols and an inner cross of 5. The outer ring turns by 2 places, then 6, then 2, so next it turns 6 places; B, C and D all show that ring, while A's ring is different and its quartered circle is tilted. The centre alternates between the dotted circle and the thick ring, so the fifth figure has the dotted circle, which rules out D. The last time the ring turned 6 places, the four inner symbols rotated one step clockwise; doing that to the fourth figure gives B.

questions.text:
A polygonal shape moves through a series of numbered tiles as shown in the figure. The shape transforms itself at every tile according to rules given below. There can be one or more transformations on any given tile. Choose the resultant polygon from the options below.

i. At even numbers one side gets added to the shape.
ii. At odd numbers two sides get removed from the shape.
iii. If the number is divisible by 2, one side gets added to the shape.
iv. If the number is divisible by 3, one side is removed from the shape.
v. On reaching the first prime number the colour of the shape changes to yellow.
vi. On reaching a second prime number the colour of the shape changes to orange.
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: The red pentagon (5 sides) passes tiles 4, 9, 8, 5, 2, 7, 6, 1, 2. An even tile adds 2 sides (rules i and iii), an odd tile removes 2, and a multiple of 3 removes one more. Sides: 4 gives 7, 9 gives 4, 8 gives 6, 5 gives 4, 2 gives 6, 7 gives 4, 6 gives 5, 1 gives 3, and 2 gives 5. The first prime, 5, turns it yellow and the second, 2, turns it orange, so the result is an orange pentagon.

questions.text: Three sides, each with circles and connecting lines, show three faces of a three-dimensional cube. (An example of such a cube is shown on the right.) Choose the correct option that corresponds to a cube with the three sides shown below.
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.subtopic: Matching a part to the whole
questions.solution: Each face is a 4 by 4 grid, and neighbouring faces share their edge circles. The bottom row of the top side matches the top row of the left side, the right column of the top side matches the top row of the right side read the other way, and the right column of the left side matches the left column of the right side, so the three sides fit together in the orientation drawn. A has two wrong circles on the right face and D two wrong circles on the left face. B and C have every circle right, but B leaves out the line on the front vertical edge joining the white corner circle to the black circle below it, which both the left side and the right side show. So C is the cube.

questions.text: From the given options, choose the correct shoe sole that pairs with the sole shown on the left.
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: The other shoe of a pair has a sole that is the mirror image of this one. Flip the given sole left to right: the big circle moves to the left of the forefoot and the zigzag band of the heel runs down the right side. All four options have the flipped forefoot layout, so compare the details. A's heel pattern differs from the flipped heel, and B and D each have a stretch of tread lines in the forefoot that does not match. C matches the flipped sole throughout.

questions.text: A circular palette with three pigment colours of the same quantity are mixed in the sequence shown below. Choose the correct resultant colour from the options.
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: Mix each third of the palette separately. Top: yellow, blue and yellow give a yellowish green. Lower left: blue, red and yellow, all three pigment primaries in equal amounts, give a dark brown, close to black. Lower right: red, yellow and yellow give a yellowish orange. D shows yellow green, dark brown and yellow orange. A's brown is too light, B's top is a dark green and C's orange is too red.

questions.text: Figure 1 shows the top view of a lawn sprinkler. The Swastika-shaped arms rotate freely around a central pivot which supplies water to the arms. Water is sprinkled through the nozzles located at the end of the arms, which causes the sprinkler head to rotate. Now, imagine the whole sprinkler submerged under water and imagine the water being aspirated (suctioned) instead of being expelled. Which direction will the sprinkler head rotate?

options.label: C
options.text: It will not rotate at all.

options.label: D
options.text: It will shuffle between clock-wise & anti-clock-wise rotations.

questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: This is the reverse sprinkler problem. When water is pushed out, each jet pushes its arm backwards and the head turns one way. When water is sucked in, the inflow gives a much weaker push, and careful experiments show the head turning slowly the other way. For these arms that is anticlockwise, so the answer is A.

questions.text: Four spheres are merged as shown in the box. After merging, the portion that is common to all of them (i.e. intersection) is removed. Identify the removed portion from the options given below.
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.subtopic: Matching a part to the whole
questions.solution: The region inside all four spheres lies where the spheres overlap most, around their common centre. It is bounded by four curved faces, one from each sphere, which meet along curved edges. Picture the four spheres in the box and find the solid bounded only by the inner parts of their surfaces. IIT Bombay's final key gives C.

questions.text: Identify which of the musical instruments mentioned below use(s) the technique of hammering on strings to produce sounds: Santoor, Piano, Harmonium and Keyboard.
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: The santoor is played by striking its strings with a pair of light wooden mallets, and in a piano each key throws a felt hammer against the strings. A harmonium makes sound with reeds vibrated by air from the bellows, and an electronic keyboard makes sound electronically, so neither hammers strings.

questions.text: A point P is placed at a distance of 12 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 17 cm. How many integer length chords of this circle can pass through P?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: The shortest chord through P is perpendicular to the radius through P, with length \(2\sqrt{17^2-12^2} = 2\sqrt{145}\), about 24.08 cm. The longest is the diameter, 34 cm. So the integer lengths possible are 25 to 34. Each length from 25 to 33 is taken by two chords, one on each side of the line through the centre and P, giving 18 chords, and the diameter gives 1 more, so 19 chords.

questions.text: Given below are images drawn with the same set of equations but with different parameters. The parameters used to generate a figure are given below the figure. Identify the correct set of parameters which would generate the figure shown on the right.
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: In the examples the number of lobes equals R divided by r: 10/2 gives 5, 16/4 gives 4 and 108/4 gives 27. The figure on the right is a rounded shape with 3 gentle lobes, so R/r must be 3. Only A gives 24/8 = 3, while B gives 4, C gives 2 and D gives 8.

questions.text:
Choose the set of words that will correctly complete the following ten sentences from the word sets given in the answer options.

I. The unnecessarily complex plot left me (bemused / amused).
II. The dispute should be resolved by a (disinterested / uninterested) judge.
III. A cup of hot coffee after a long day is (enervating / energizing).
IV. She (depreciated / deprecated) his efforts.
V. He (flaunted / flouted) the rules.
VI. The new batsman (floundered / foundered) initially, but recovered after sometime.
VII. By a (fortunate / fortuitous) coincidence, I met my old friend at the mall.
VIII. The rebels were (interned / interred) in the military jail.
IX. The artist had a (luxurious / luxuriant) imagination.
X. His (simplistic / simple) answer suggested he wasn't familiar with the material.

options.label: A
options.text: bemused, disinterested, energizing, deprecated, flouted, floundered, fortunate, interred, luxurious, simplistic.

options.label: B
options.text: amused, uninterested, enervating, depreciated, flouted, foundered, fortuitous, interned, luxuriant, simple.

options.label: C
options.text: bemused, disinterested, energizing, deprecated, flouted, floundered, fortuitous, interned, luxuriant, simplistic.

options.label: D
options.text: amused, disinterested, enervating, depreciated, flaunted, foundered, fortuitous, interned, luxurious, simple.

questions.subject: Language
questions.solution: A confusing plot leaves you bemused (puzzled), a judge should be disinterested (impartial), coffee is energizing (enervating means draining), to deprecate is to express disapproval, rules are flouted (flaunt means show off), a batsman who struggles flounders (founder means sink), a chance meeting is fortuitous, prisoners are interned (interred means buried), a rich imagination is luxuriant and an over-simple answer is simplistic. Only C has all ten.

questions.text: Given below is a sequence of shapes arranged from left to right. There are eight rules which, when applied to the sequence, will transform it to one of the four options shown below. Identify the correct option.
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: The start is: square with tick, square with cross, circle with cross, circle with slash, circle with dot, circle with three dots, square with caret, circle with bar. Applying the rules in the order of the sum: swap 3rd and 6th; turn the cross-in-square into a cross-in-circle; reverse the sequence; swap 5th and 2nd; replace each square by the circle before it; swap 4th and 7th. This gives circle with bar, circle with slash, cross circle, cross circle, dot circle, three-dot circle, dot circle, cross circle. Last, the two cross circles stand together, so the first of them swaps with the first shape, giving cross circle, slash circle, bar circle, cross circle, dot circle, three-dot circle, dot circle, cross circle, which is D. A is the sequence before this last step.

questions.text: Which of the options given below will correctly complete the series?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: The panels are numbered 1, 2, 3, 4 going clockwise, so the empty one is panel 3. Each panel has a star, a polygon, a white circle and a black circle. The star's points go 4, 6, ?, 10 and the polygon's sides go 9, 7, ?, 3, so panel 3 needs an 8-pointed star and a pentagon. Star and polygon colours alternate between white and black, giving a white star and a black polygon. Moving each item on around the panel puts the polygon top left, the black circle top right, the white circle bottom left and the star bottom right, which is D.

questions.text: Five figures are coded with symbols, as shown below. From the given options, find the code for Figure 1.
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: Compare which symbols the figures share. The yin-yang symbol appears exactly where there is a triangle, the wave symbol where there are lines, the drop where there are two or more black dots, and the crossed box where there are four black shapes. Figure 1 has lines, a black triangle, three black dots and four black shapes in all, so its code needs the drop, the wave, the crossed box and the yin-yang. Only B has all four.

questions.text: Identify the option that can be assembled to form Figure 1.
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Figure 1 is a block E: two units wide and five units tall with two one-unit notches, so its area is 8 square units, or 32 half-unit squares. All four option sets are drawn at the same scale. Measured in half-unit squares, the bricks in A add up to 30 (15 bricks of 2), the pieces in B to 30 (10 + 10 + 2 + 8) and the L-shapes and rectangle in D to 30 (7 + 5 + 6 + 5 + 7). Only the pink pieces in C add up to 32 (12 + 8 + 6 + 4 + 2), the area of the E, and their 45 degree edges pair up to make its square corners.

questions.text:
Read the following statements related to the economy.

I. Devaluation of a currency means fixing the value of currency in multilateral consultation with the IMF, the World Bank, and major trading partners.
II. The Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility states that as you keep on consuming a commodity continuously, the satisfaction derived from each subsequent unit will keep falling.
III. Since human wants are unlimited and available resources are limited, a rational consumer will try to satisfy the least urgent needs which can be met within his/her income levels.
IV. Budget deficit means the difference between all receipts and all expenditure.

Which of the above statements are TRUE?
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: Statement II is the law of diminishing marginal utility as usually stated, and IV is the definition of a budget deficit (total expenditure minus total receipts). Statement I is false: devaluation is a deliberate lowering of a currency's official value, not a value fixed in consultation with the IMF and the World Bank. Statement III is false: a rational consumer satisfies the most urgent needs first. So II and IV are true.

questions.text:
Given below is a list of sixteen idioms connected with water. Each of the four options contains meanings of four randomly selected idioms from the list. Identify the option that contains correct meanings for all four of the chosen idioms.

I. Fish out of water
II. Tread water
III. Come hell or high water
IV. Watershed moment
V. Pour oil in troubled waters
VI. Throw the baby out with the bath water
VII. Watering hole
VIII. Head above water
IX. Carry water for someone
X. Water under the bridge
XI. Uncharted waters
XII. Muddy the waters
XIII. Mouth watering
XIV. In deep water
XV. Dip your toe in the water
XVI. Water down

options.label: A
options.text: tavern, past, make progress, in trouble

options.label: B
options.text: confuse or complicate the situation, to help, dilute, make matters worse

options.label: C
options.text: tentative step, persistent in the face of difficulty, tasty, survive

options.label: D
options.text: turning point, new territory, discard bad with good, misfit

questions.subject: Language
questions.solution: C matches four idioms exactly: dip your toe in the water (tentative step), come hell or high water (persistent in the face of difficulty), mouth watering (tasty) and head above water (survive). A fails because tread water means making no progress. B fails because pouring oil on troubled waters means calming a situation, not making it worse. D fails because throwing the baby out with the bath water means discarding the good along with the bad.

questions.text: Shown below are different handle positions of a hand tool. Identify which handle position gives the most comfortable hand posture for a downward to-and-fro motion.
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: When you push a saw forward and down, the forearm slopes down toward the tool and the wrist is most comfortable kept straight. A fist holds a handle roughly across the forearm, so the handle should lean back over the blade, as in B, which lines the forearm up with the downward push. A straight handle (A) forces the wrist to bend, while a vertical handle (C) or one leaning away from the blade (D) suits a level or upward push.

questions.text: A pilot has to fly direct from Mumbai to Singapore. The departure of the flight from Mumbai airport is at dusk. Which colour goggles should the pilot be wearing at Mumbai airport for quickly adapting to darkness after take-off?
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: The rods in the eye, which give night vision, are almost insensitive to red light. Red goggles let the cones handle the bright scene while the rods stay dark adapted, so the pilot sees well in the dark soon after take-off. Blue light strongly bleaches the rods, and black or brown lenses only dim all colours without protecting rod adaptation in the same way.

questions.text: Here is a sketch of Alka with her mouth missing. Choose the correct sequence from the mouth shapes given below that will allow Alka to say “WELCOME TO UCEED”.
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Say the phrase sound by sound: W (pursed lips, 5), E (open smile with teeth, 4), L (open mouth with tongue up, 2), CO (open round mouth, 6), M (lips closed, 1), TO (small tall oval, 8), U (small round pucker, 3) and CEED (teeth together, lips stretched, 7). That gives 5, 4, 2, 6, 1, 8, 3, 7. The other sequences put the closed lips for M or the opening W in the wrong place.

questions.text:
If the following passage describing a situation was to be made into a comic page, match the numbered dialogues with the appropriate bubble according to comic book conventions:

Meanwhile at the college canteen, the manager was livid (1). “How many times have I told you to keep track of the orders?” (2), He screamed at the helpless waiter. Everyone stood still and watched. “What happened? Why is he screaming?” (3), I turned around to ask the person behind me in the queue at the counter. He bent forward and whispered, “Nothing new…he screams at everybody all the time. His staff hate him for that” (4). “Oh, that’s not fair!” (5), I thought to myself, while the manager got louder and louder.
questions.subject: Language
questions.solution: In comics, narration goes in a rectangular caption box (d), a shout in a spiky burst (b), normal speech in a plain oval with a tail (c), a whisper in a dashed bubble (a), and a thought in a cloud with small trailing circles (e). So 1 is narration (d), 2 is shouted (b), 3 is spoken (c), 4 is whispered (a) and 5 is thought (e).

questions.text:
Arrange the following video formats according to their evolution:
Beta, U-matic low band, VHS, Digibeta, U-matic Hi band

options.label: A
options.text: VHS, U-matic low band, U-matic hi band, Beta, Digibeta

options.label: B
options.text: U-matic low band, U-matic hi band, Beta, Digibeta, VHS

options.label: C
options.text: Digibeta, Beta, U-matic hi band, U-matic low band, VHS

options.label: D
options.text: Beta, Digibeta, U-matic low band, U-matic Hi band, VHS

questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: U-matic low band came first, in 1971; VHS followed in 1976, then U-matic high band, Betacam (Beta) in 1982 and Digital Betacam in 1993. A and B both keep U-matic low band, U-matic high band, Beta and Digibeta in order; A puts VHS first and B puts it last. IIT Bombay's final key gives A.
questions.defect: As printed, no option gives the true order. U-matic (low band) came in 1971 and VHS in 1976, followed by U-matic high band, Betacam (Beta) in 1982 and Digital Betacam (Digibeta) in 1993. IIT Bombay's final key gives A.

questions.text: Black & white photographs of the bin shown in Picture 1 were shot using red, yellow, and green colour filters. An additional black & white photograph was shot without any filter. From the given options, identify the photograph shot using red filter.
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: A colour filter passes its own colour and blocks its opposite, so in a black and white photo it lightens objects of its own colour and darkens the others. A red filter blocks almost all blue light, so the blue bin records darkest of all, while the dry, yellowish grass stays light. In C the bin is clearly the darkest of the four and the grass is bright, so C was shot with the red filter.

questions.text:
Match the cartoonist with his work.

i. Mario Miranda
ii. Sudhir Tailang
iii. Keshav
iv. R.K.Laxman
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: Mario Miranda is known for crowded, detailed street scenes full of characters (q). Sudhir Tailang drew sharp political cartoons such as the sleeping fat figure guarded by a policeman (p). Keshav of The Hindu draws loose line sketches of ordinary people talking (s). R.K. Laxman's pen drawings include railway station scenes like the one in r.

questions.text: Here are two sketches of Priyanka standing in front of a mirror. Spot the differences in the two sketches, and choose the correct number of differences from the options given below:
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Compare the sketches region by region. Differences found: (1) a mole beside the nose in the left sketch only, (2) an extra hoop earring in the right sketch, (3) a round bag buckle on the left versus a square one on the right, (4) the straw of the blender jar on the dresser is shaped differently, (5) the blue box has light walls and a dark screen on the left but dark walls and a light screen on the right, (6) the yellow jar has an orange label band on the left only, and (7) the fingers of the hand holding the bag are drawn differently. That makes 7 differences.

questions.text: Given below are top views of a straight path along which a man moves in different ways. The dots represent the positions where his feet touch the ground. Choose the correct option that represents a dog running fast:
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: A dog running fast gallops: the two hind feet land almost together, then the two front feet land one just after the other, followed by a long leap. B shows hind legs landing together and front legs slightly staggered, which is the gallop. A pairs diagonal legs (a trot), C lands both hind and then both front feet exactly together (a bound) and D lands all four feet together (a hop).

questions.text:
A colour picked in a paint software had the following values (RGB mode): Red=255, Green=100, Blue=0

The colour picked was:
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: Full red with a little green and no blue makes orange. Equal red and green at full strength would give yellow, and grey needs all three values equal. Brown is a dark orange, so it needs a red value well below 255.

questions.text:
Read the text given below and answer the question that follows.

This (presence of benefits) together with (four) reasons
Is what the Tathāgata himself explained
In (the sūtra) requested by Subāhu
For the benefit of those inclined toward the lesser (paths).

If a person with a helpful intention
Thinks, “I shall merely relieve
The headaches of (a few) beings,”
(And this thought) is (already) endowed with boundless merit,

Then it is needless to mention that
Wishing to dispel the boundless misery of every single being,
And wishing for each of them
To accomplish boundless qualities (also carries boundless merit).

Do even fathers and mothers
Have such a benefiting intention?
Do the gods and sages
Or even Brahma have it?

Which philosophical tradition does this text belong to?
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: Tathāgata is a title of the Buddha, a sūtra is a Buddhist discourse, and the wish to remove the misery of every being is the bodhisattva ideal; the verses are from Shantideva's Bodhicaryavatara. Jainism calls its teachers Tirthankaras, not Tathāgata, and the Advaita and Dvaita schools of Vedanta are Hindu traditions that would not set Brahma below this intention.

questions.text: Climate scientists tell us that such extremes of weather as the floods in Chennai or the acute lack of rainfall in large parts of India are due to a phenomenon called El Niño. The name comes from:

options.label: A
options.text: "The boy child" or baby Jesus, because it happens around Christmas time.

options.label: B
options.text: "The fiery storm"—for the hurricanes that occur in Central and South America from September through December.

options.label: C
options.text: "The bubbling sea"—named by fishermen for the huge waves that accompany dramatically varying temperature patterns.

options.label: D
options.text: "The death zone"—named by scientists for the large numbers of marine animals that die on the Pacific coasts of the Americas, because of the seas warming up.

questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: El Niño is Spanish for the boy child. Peruvian fishermen gave the name to the warm current that appeared off their coast around Christmas, in honour of the infant Jesus. The other options invent meanings: the name has nothing to do with storms, waves or a death zone.

questions.text: The Vikram and Vetala series of stories, well-known across India, originate in the:

options.label: A
options.text: Mahabhasya, perhaps of the 2nd century BCE

options.label: B
options.text: Ubhayabhisarika, perhaps of the 4th-6th centuries CE

options.label: C
options.text: Katha-sarita-sagara, perhaps of the 11th century CE

options.label: D
options.text: Sukasaptati, perhaps of the 12th century CE

questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: The Vetala Panchavimshati, the twenty-five tales the Vetala tells King Vikrama, is preserved in Somadeva's Katha-sarita-sagara of the 11th century. The Mahabhasya is Patanjali's grammar commentary, the Ubhayabhisarika is a short play, and the Sukasaptati is a separate collection of seventy tales told by a parrot.

questions.text: If a ball is placed in front of two mirrors at right angles to each other, as shown in the image, how many reflections will the ball generate?
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: Two plane mirrors at an angle of \(\theta\) form \(360/\theta - 1\) images when \(360/\theta\) is even. With the mirrors at 90 degrees this gives 4 minus 1, which is 3: one image in each mirror and a third image seen in the corner, made by reflection from both mirrors.

questions.text: For the object shown in the box, which option identifies the position of its center of gravity correctly?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: The T has a top bar 2x wide and x tall (area 2x squared) and a centred stem x wide and 2x tall (area 2x squared), with the same thickness throughout. It is symmetric left to right, so the centre of gravity is on the middle line. Measured from the bottom, the bar's centre is at 2.5x and the stem's at x; with equal areas the centre of gravity is halfway, at 1.75x, which is 0.25x below the joint of bar and stem. Only D places the dot a little way down the stem, just under the bar.

questions.text: The image in the box shows a 3D object. From among the options below, select the one that shows the same object from a different view.
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: The object is a hub with four arms, each ending in a notched plate. Turn the object in your mind to each option's viewpoint and check every plate in turn: which side its notch is on and which way the plate faces. Option C shows the same object from another side; in each of the others one plate is notched or turned the wrong way.

questions.text:
The circles in the image contain letters from F to V for purposes of identification of points. Directions are encoded in the statements below in such a way that NE stands for North-East, NNE for North-North-East, and so on. If all the following statements are true, select the correct representation of these statements from the given options.

- M is in NNE of G and L is in SSW of N
- P is in NW of K and U is in SSE of O
- V is in ESE of P and F is in NNW of S
- H is in SW of V and O is in NNE of J
- I is in SSE of N and Q is in SE of M
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: Fix the fixed ones first: P is NW of K, so K is the outer SE point; V is ESE of P, so V is the inner ESE circle; I is SSE of N, which needs N at the outer NE and I at the outer E. Options C and D fail here (C has V in the outer ring and N inside; in D, G is not SW of M so M cannot be NNE of G). In A, U is not SSE of O and H is not SW of V. B satisfies all the other statements: M NNE of G, L SSW of N, U SSE of O, F NNW of S, H SW of V and Q SE of M.

questions.text:
Select the option that has the correct match.

p) Ramsar Convention 1971
q) Vienna Convention 1981
r) Montreal Protocol 1989
s) Kyoto Protocol 1995

i) Unite countries to pursue sustainable development
ii) Reduce GHG emissions
iii) Conservation and sustainable utilisation of wetlands
iv) Protection of the ozone layer
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: Match each treaty with its aim: Ramsar (1971) conserves wetlands, the Vienna Convention and the Montreal Protocol protect the ozone layer, and the Kyoto Protocol reduces greenhouse gas emissions. D's first pair, q-iv, is right, but its second, r-i, is not. IIT Bombay's final key gives D.
questions.defect: As printed, no option is fully correct: the Ramsar Convention (wetlands) is p-iii, the Vienna Convention and the Montreal Protocol both protect the ozone layer (q-iv, r-iv), and the Kyoto Protocol reduces greenhouse gas emissions (s-ii); the printed years are also wrong (Vienna 1985, Montreal 1987, Kyoto 1997). IIT Bombay's final key gives D.

questions.text: There are four bins labelled ‘i’ to ‘iv’ as shown below. If the objects labelled ‘p’ to ‘y’ are to be thrown in their respective bins, which of the following combinations is correct.
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: The bins are for organic waste (i, leaves), toxic waste (ii, skull), recyclables (iii, recycling arrows) and other or caution waste (iv, warning sign). In B the chemical flask goes to toxic (r-ii), the apple core to organic (t-i), the old T-shirt to other waste (x-iv), and the plastic bottle and paper cup to recycling (s-iii, p-iii). A puts a toothbrush in organic and a T-shirt in toxic, C puts a sock in toxic, and D puts a plastic bottle in organic.

questions.text:
Given below are some statements about rock-cut architecture. Which of these is TRUE?

i. A lot of religious architecture was built or cut out of rock during the Vedic age; the remains of rudimentary sacrificial altars are evidence of the same.
ii. Rock-cut temples were hollowed out of mountains or seams carved out of hard stone, but have more in common with conventional buildings constructed with blocks of dressed stone than with sculpture.
iii. The transition from the earlier wooden to stone buildings resulted in “petrification” of forms; the heritage of the earlier periods was carefully transcribed into new materials.
iv. The gigantic Kailasa temple at Ellora is the kind of rock-cut architecture—exactly as the rathas at Mamallapuram—where the monolithic building was carved straight out of living rock to create an occupiable space.
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: Early rock-cut caves copied the forms of timber buildings in stone, down to imitation rafters and beams, so iii is true. Statement i is false: Vedic religion used temporary brick or earth altars, not rock-cut buildings. Statement ii is false: carving a temple out of rock is closer to sculpture than to building with dressed blocks. Statement iv fails because the rathas at Mamallapuram are solid monoliths, not occupiable spaces, so they are not exactly like the Kailasa temple.

questions.text: Below is a set of pictures that show the variety of arches used in Islamic architecture in India from 7th to 17th centuries CE. Select the order in which the design of the arch developed.
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: The earliest arches in India were corbelled, built from overlapping horizontal courses as in iv (Quwwat-ul-Islam screen, late 12th century). The first true arch with radiating voussoirs came with decorative fringes on the underside, as in i (Alai Darwaza, early 14th century). Plainer pointed true arches like iii followed under the later Sultanates, and the scalloped multi-foil arch ii is a Mughal form of the 17th century. So the order is iv, i, iii, ii.

questions.text: Which disease is caused by the deficiency of proteins?
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: Kwashiorkor is caused mainly by a lack of protein, even when calories are enough, and shows as swelling and a bloated belly. Marasmus is a shortage of total energy (calories and protein together), pellagra is a deficiency of niacin (vitamin B3), and anorexia is an eating disorder or loss of appetite, not a protein deficiency.

questions.text: The word given below is written in a specific font. From the options, choose the word that belongs to the same font family.
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Compare the design of the given word with each option: the weight and contrast of the strokes, the shape of the ends of strokes, and how the curves are drawn. Words in the same font family share these features even when the script or weight differs. Option B has the same construction as the given word, while A, C and D are built differently.
